top_signals.title: Soft US Jobs Cast Doubt on September Fed Hike
top_signals.summary: Jennifer McKeown, Chief Global Economist at Capital Economics, discussed the implications of the recent US labor market report on Federal Reserve interest rate expectations. The report showed a decline in payrolls alongside a drop in the unemployment rate, presenting a mixed picture. Wage growth at 3.2% was softer than expected, which may reduce the likelihood of an imminent rate hike in September. McKeown emphasized that the upcoming July CPI data and the next payroll report before the September Fed meeting will be critical in shaping policy decisions. She also highlighted concerns about the falling labor force participation rate, questioning whether this reflects structural issues or a mismatch between job quality and worker preferences. Overall, the segment underscored market uncertainty ahead of key inflation data that will influence the Fed's next moves. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.
